route: 1 (published per-item factor loadings, additional online Table 2), EFA re-run + nearest-neighbour
evidence: Route 1-analogue on published factor loadings (the paper's additional online Table 2, 'Oblimin-Rotated Factor Loadings of the Three Adjective Narcissism Scales', in Supplementary materials (Study 1 and Study 2).docx, OSF u93eq). Re-ran the paper's 3-factor principal-axis oblimin EFA over all 42 adjectives with the LIVE IRW nas_rogoza_2024_study2_nvs responses in place of the .sav's NVS1-11 columns (N=353, live id i = .sav row i, guarded). Published vs observed (Neurotic/Antagonistic/Agentic): NVS1 Ashamed .61/.13/.00 vs .60/.14/.01 (d=0.015); NVS2 Ignored .79/-.06/-.01 vs .79/-.05/.00 (0.020); NVS3 Self-absorbed .27/.25/.05 vs .28/.25/.05 (0.007); NVS4 Fragile .66/-.08/-.02 vs .65/-.07/-.01 (0.022); NVS5 Underappreciated .65/-.01/.00 vs .64/.00/.01 (0.018); NVS6 Envious .75/.02/.03 vs .75/.03/.04 (0.016); NVS7 Resentful .72/.12/.00 vs .72/.13/.01 (0.010); NVS8 Insecure .87/-.13/-.10 vs .86/-.12/-.09 (0.022); NVS9 Irritable .68/.09/-.07 vs .68/.10/-.06 (0.011); NVS10 Misunderstood .66/.06/.02 vs .66/.07/.02 (0.010); NVS11 Vengeful .27/.41/.05 vs .28/.41/.06 (0.012). Nearest-neighbour matching against ALL 42 published triples returns the identity permutation, 11/11. Worst deviation 0.022; minimum pairwise separation among the 11 NVS published triples 0.073 (Fragile vs Underappreciated), margin 3.30x, so every item is distinguished from every other item and not merely assigned to the neurotic block. NOT established by this route: the option_text<->resp axis -- the 1='Not at all' / 7='Extremely' anchors come from the codebook's own printed scale and involve no inference, and the six intermediate points are unlabelled in the source. Also not established: anything about the 31 non-NVS adjectives, whose responses were read from the source .sav rather than from IRW.

Route 8 (mean level, live IRW data): per-item means NAS1 12.923 / NAS2 16.152 / NAS3 12.932 / NAS4 12.431 and %-at-zero 52.70 / 47.27 / 54.72 / 54.86. NAS2 leads the next-highest by 3.219 points on a 0-100 slider and is the only one below 52% floored, which pins it to Lekceważący ('dismissive/depreciating'), by far the mildest of the four adjectives. Route 1 (cross-study nomological profile; Study 2's 18 code->adjective pairs were verified item-by-item in batch_114 against additional online Table 2's published loadings): d = cor(item, NVS composite) - cor(item, NGS composite), computed on the live IRW study5 nas/nvs/ngs tables joined on id+wave (8,199 person-occasions), gives NAS1 0.339 / NAS2 0.309 / NAS3 0.183 / NAS4 0.225; the minimum is NAS3, and in Study 2 Exploitative is the unique one of the four with a NEGATIVE d (-0.073, against Abusive +0.144, Depreciating +0.200, Nasty +0.141), i.e. the only adjective of the four tilting grandiose rather than vulnerable -- so NAS3 = Wyzyskujący/Exploitative. Over all 24 code->adjective assignments the shipped one (Abusive Depreciating Exploitative Nasty) scores Spearman rho=0.80 against the Study 2 d profile, rank 2 of 24 (tied), while the leading rival -- the order the same four items appear in on the final 16-item NAS form (Abusive Nasty Exploitative Depreciating) -- scores 0.40. Plumbing corroboration, not mapping: the authors' Mplus 'CFA DD.out' reports NAS1..NAS4 n = 8212/8210/8206/8204, equal to the live per-item n exactly, and means 12.919/16.150/12.929/12.430, matching live to 0.004. NOT established, hence PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED: NAS1 vs NAS4 (Znieważający/Abusive vs Bezczelny/Nasty) are not distinguished by any route -- 12.923 vs 12.431 live means, d 0.339 vs 0.225, and their Study 2 anchors sit 0.003 apart in d and 0.08 apart in mean; a swap of those two would be invisible.

Routes 5 + 1/8 + rival-ordering elimination, run on the live table (verify_nas_rogoza_2024_study5_ngs.R, VERDICT: PASS). Claim: NGS1=Genialny/Brilliant, NGS2=Wspanialy/Glorious, NGS3=Potezny/Powerful, NGS4=Prestizowy/Prestigious, which splits the four into a self-excellence pair {NGS1,NGS2} and a status pair {NGS3,NGS4}. CHECK 1 (block structure, 9510 observations): claimed within-pair r NGS1-NGS2 0.814 and NGS3-NGS4 0.730; cross-pair NGS1-NGS3 0.676, NGS1-NGS4 0.622, NGS2-NGS3 0.721, NGS2-NGS4 0.663; min within 0.730 > max cross 0.721 -- passes, but by only 0.009, which is the weakest link in this row. CHECK 1b (rival elimination, decisive): Edershile & Wright (2021), the ESM study these four items were taken from, list them Glorious, Prestigious, Brilliant, Powerful; that ordering implies pairs {NGS1,NGS3} r=0.676 and {NGS2,NGS4} r=0.663, both far below the 0.814 it would have to treat as a cross-pair correlation, so it is ruled out. CHECK 2 (item location, clean): means 32.381 / 32.924 / 24.477 / 23.427 and %-at-floor 24.34 / 22.96 / 36.42 / 38.96 -- the claimed excellence pair is endorsed higher and floors less than the claimed status pair, with a 7.9-point gap and no overlap. CHECK 3 (code axis only, corroboration): the deposit's own Mplus output 'CFA DD.out' publishes per-code n, mean, skew and %-at-zero; live vs published is exact for all four -- n 8201/8196/8194/8192, means 32.381/32.924/24.477/23.427, largest mean deviation 0.0004. That confirms live item NGSk is .sav column NGSk; it establishes nothing about the adjective. NOT ESTABLISHED: Brilliant vs Glorious, and Powerful vs Prestigious. Every check above is symmetric within a pair, so 8 of the 24 possible orderings survive -- hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. The order itself rests on three agreeing textual sources (Study 5 daily codebook, the paper's Measures paragraph, Study 6 state codebook), none of which ties an adjective to a column code.

route: 1+8 (per-item means vs the authors' own Study 2 administration of the same adjectives); 5 (correlation-permutation matching, negative/underpowered)
evidence: Live table fetched and reduced to 317 person-level means (32,868 non-missing responses). Anchor: the same authors' Study 2 English trait administration of the same four NVS adjectives (OSF u93eq 'Study 2 NAS.sav', N=353, 1-7), where Misunderstood 3.105 and Underappreciated 3.334 sit above Ignored 2.629 and Resentful 2.252. Live Study 5 person means under the shipped mapping: NVS1=Ignored 19.261, NVS2=Resentful 18.813, NVS3=Misunderstood 25.347, NVS4=Underappreciated 21.999. All four block contrasts hold: NVS3-NVS1 +6.09 (t=11.72, p=1.4e-26), NVS3-NVS2 +6.53 (t=14.46, p=9.7e-37), NVS4-NVS1 +2.74 (t=4.82, p=2.2e-06), NVS4-NVS2 +3.19 (t=6.25, p=1.3e-09) -- a prediction that fails for 20 of the 24 possible permutations. What this does NOT establish: NVS1 vs NVS2 is +0.45, t=1.20, p=0.23 (Ignored and Resentful are not separated), and NVS3-NVS4 = +3.35 is the REVERSE of Study 2's Misunderstood-vs- Underappreciated rank, so the within-block assignment is not verified either. Route 5 was run and is a negative: matching the 4x4 between-person correlation matrix against Study 2's over all 24 permutations ranks the shipped mapping 18th (r=-0.235 vs best +0.828), but the six live correlations span only 0.824-0.908, so the ranking is noise from a single dominant factor and is not read as counter-evidence. Within-block order therefore rests on document order in three of the study's own texts (Study 5 daily codebook, Study 6 state codebook, article Study 5 Measures paragraph), not on data. Separately, the Polish-English adjective crosswalk is fixed at the source: the Study 2 codebook's English 42-adjective pool and the Study 3 codebook's Polish 40-adjective pool are the same list in the same order and their NVS blocks align 11/11. Re-runnable as verify_nas_rogoza_2024_study5_nvs.R (VERDICT: PASS).
